        "title": "ARC fill gaps between aligned markers",
        "content": "In ARC tasks with sparse marker dots (e.g. color 0 on background 9), change only background cells to color 3 when they lie strictly between two marker cells in the same row or same column. Preserve all marker cells and all background cells outside such horizontal/vertical spans. Compute consecutive markers per row and column and fill the intervening cells. Do not include diagonals.       "fill_aligned_gaps_between_matching_markers": {

        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "Fill aligned gaps between matching markers",
        "content": "Continual-ARC rule: in a grid with a uniform background and sparse marker color, recolor background cells between markers sharing a row or column. For each background cell, if there is a marker somewhere strictly to its left and strictly to its right in the same row, or strictly above and below in the same column, recolor it to color 3. Keep markers and cells without such a pair unchanged. Markers may be multiple; endpoints are simply first/last aligned marker, filling all intervening background gaps.",

      "arc_collinear_marker_gap_fill": {

        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC collinear marker gap fill",
        "content": "ARC pattern with sparse marker color and background: recolor background to 3 in straight row/column gaps between same-color markers, preserving marker cells. Demonstrations confirm: row/column gaps (e.g. 5x24 row0 markers c9,13,15,17,21 fill each intervening span; 4x12 column c3 markers r1,r10 fill r2-r9; 5x14 row5 c0,c4 fills c1-c3, and col4 r5,r9 fills r6-r8). Important caveat: naively filling every collinear gap failed on a test containing many markers, despite this rule; task likely has a selection constraint/pattern not identified. Do not assume background blanket-recolor. Request demos to learn which aligned marker pairs qualify.",

        "title": "Fill spaces between aligned identical markers",
        "content": "Continual-ARC rule confirmed by task-bf0baebd: in a uniform background grid with sparse identical marker cells (demo: marker 5 on background 8, output fill 3; test: marker 6 on background 0, fill 3), recolor background cells strictly between successive markers along each row or column. Leave marker cells and cells outside such aligned gaps unchanged. Take the union of horizontal and vertical gaps; intersections remain fill color. For each row/column, sort marker positions and fill between consecutive occurrences (equivalently, every background cell with another marker beyond it in at least one direction on the same row or column).         "title": "ARC paired panels: mark aligned shared-color matches",
        "content": "Continual-ARC task-98c968f1: Grid has two equal-sized panels separated by a uniform divider (horizontal or vertical); output is aligned panel-sized grid. Compare cells at same coordinates. In the solved instance, left panel colors 4/6, right panel 1/6; output was all 6, with 3 at the sole coordinate where both panels contained 6. Be cautious: the task may use panels split horizontally or vertically; separator indicates axis. In demo7, output marks aligned shared 4s and background 4.         "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC divider halves with sparse recoloring (task-98c968f1)",
        "content": "Task-98c968f1 demonstrations show a grid split by a uniform separator row/column; output is the section on one side, but orientation/color rule is not reliably inferred from current observations. Demos: (1) 15x10, separator row 7 color6, output 7x10 from rows 8-14; source lower section background9 with sparse0 becomes background3/sparse9. (2) 19x6 separator row9 color5, output 9x6 from rows10-18; source 8/0 becomes 0/3 respectively. (3) 29x19 separator col9 color1, output 29x9 from cols0-8; source region 4/9/1 and output mostly9 with sparse3. (4) 11x25 separator row5 color7, output top 5 rows. (5) 22x17 separator col8 color0, output left 8 cols; source top-left section 1/6 maps base6 and sparse marks3. (6) 11x24 separator row5 color6, output top5 rows; source top section 0/1 maps 0->1,1->3. General takeaway: output half orientation varies across demos and color mapping varies; identify from demonstrative correspondence rather than assume lower half. Test has 29x2, row14 [0,0] separator, upper 14 rows colors8/1 and lower14 colors4/1. Tried multiple plausible output halves/mappings, all wrong; no solved rule. Avoid blindly extrapolating.",

        "title": "Separated panels noisy-halves ARC puzzle",

      "arc_periodic_completion_from_sparse_diagonal_row_signals": {
        "id": "arc_periodic_completion_from_sparse_diagonal_row_signals",
        "kind": "memory",
